children: Bank of America says Apple's latest flagship iPhones are reaching customers in much the same timeframe as last year, with delivery estimates shorter for both Pro models.

Bank of America tracked order fulfillment dates across Apple's website and carrier platforms. As of now, the global average wait stood at 14 days for the iPhone 18 Pro, versus 15 days for its predecessor, while the Pro Max averaged 20 days compared with 21 days.
China showed the quickest availability among the regions reviewed. Delivery windows there were 11 days for the Pro and 15 days for the Pro Max.

The figures come alongside regional pricing differences. Apple raised prices for the 256GB Pro models by about 20% to 23% in Japan and India, while increases in China, the U.K., Germany and the U.S. ranged from 8% to 12%. Australia saw an increase of about 5%.

Bank of America retained its Buy rating and $370 price target on Apple. The bank said shipping trends were gradually improving, while noting that demand for the iPhone Duo may be affecting comparisons with last year.

title: BofA Sends Stark Message to Apple Stock Investors on iPhone 18
